item.description:

**The Defeat of the Change Bloc and the Surge in Arab Voter Turnout Increase the Chances of a Different Kind of Politics**

Last night’s exit polls sent one clear message: Netanyahu lost, but it was unclear who had won on the other side.

Here is an update as the actual results come in: Netanyahu has not yet won, but the Change Bloc has been defeated.

I have been covering politics since the beginning of the century. Never have I seen a political camp prepare for elections so impeccably, so systematically, and with such energy as the Change Bloc. Exemplary vote-sharing agreements, an unprecedented operation to fly voters in from abroad. And yet, according to the actual vote count, it ended up with roughly the same number of seats as in the previous election.

Demographics defeated energy, and the messaging also proved problematic and unsuccessful. The public was not convinced that the war had been a complete victory, but it also refused to accept the claim that it had been a complete failure. Voters were repulsed by ultra-Orthodox draft evasion, but they did not believe the solution was a minority government dependent on draft refusers and anti-Zionists. They were disgusted by the chanting of “We Do Not Believe in the Rule of the Zionists,” but they were equally shocked by the singing of “Biladi, Biladi” at the Joint List’s headquarters yesterday.

Netanyahu’s position changed dramatically between the closing of the exit polls and the emergence of the actual results. Last night, it seemed certain that the Speaker of the Knesset would be removed and that, one way or another, a minority government headed by Eisenkot would be formed.

Now, according to the criteria Eisenkot himself established, he has lost the legitimacy to form such a government. They would need the active support of the Joint List to establish it, and that seems both futile and pointless.

There is simply no chance that, in post-October 7 Israel, a coalition could survive for long with six immediate family members of people murdered by Hamas sitting alongside Knesset members who explain that Hamas is actually a charitable organization.

And so, much like Moshe Dayan once said to the Arabs, Netanyahu effectively told the Change Bloc in the early hours of the morning: “Here is my phone number. You are welcome to call.”

Lieberman, Bennett, and Eisenkot now face a dilemma from hell: head into another election, this time without the thousands of Israelis abroad rushing home to vote; attempt to join Netanyahu’s bloc under difficult conditions and in violation of their campaign promises; or go begging to Ra’am and the Joint List, both intoxicated by victory.

And one final observation: Throughout the entire election campaign, we searched for the third bloc — the unity bloc.

There were Gantz and Erdan, Winter and Zelekha, Tropper, and who even remembers who else. They all collapsed, evaporated, or disappeared.

And now, it turns out that perhaps the real unity bloc was the Arab parties all along.

Their extraordinary and historic voter turnout, at levels that will require thorough examination, shattered both sides’ dreams of reaching 61 seats.

It reminded Jews on both sides of the political divide that perhaps, after years of division, they will have to learn to sit together after all.

Main points from the speech of Hezbollah Secretary General, Naim Qassem, this evening on “the regional developments”:

1. Resistance weapons: We will continue the resistance and fight any aggression against us and against Lebanon. We will not agree to discuss disarming as long as the occupation and aggression continue. Israel must withdraw in accordance with the agreement of November 27, 2024, and Resolution 1701.

2. The framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel: We do not recognize the validity of the framework agreement. It contradicts the constitution and the Taif Agreement, gives the enemy what it is not entitled to, relinquishes Lebanon’s sources of strength, and encourages civil war.

3. The Iran–U.S. agreement: We attach great importance to the agreement between Iran and the United States, as it is a source of strength for us alongside the steadfastness of the resistance and its supporters. The agreement has already led to a reduction in aggression against Lebanon, and Iran is working to end it and to achieve an Israeli withdrawal.

4. The government in Israel: We are not interested in who governs Israel. They must know that they cannot continue to occupy our land and that they must withdraw from it.

5. American influence: We must put an end to American patronage and its control over some of the state’s institutions. Foreign patronage is akin to occupation, and both harm Lebanon’s sovereignty.

6. Rebuilding Lebanon: We are committed to continuing to provide shelter, rehabilitation, and reconstruction, using the resources at our disposal in addition to efforts to ensure that the state fulfills its obligations, with the help of friendly countries.

7. National unity: We are committed to national unity and are ready to do whatever is necessary to mend rifts and unify positions, but we also demand that others demonstrate their commitment to unity through actions.

8. The alliance with Amal and the army: Our relations with the Amal Movement and with the forces supporting the resistance are solid. ​עמודים המזוהים עם צבאו של ג'ולאני ממשיכים לפזר איומים לעבר ישראל ברקע פעילות צה"ל בדרום סוריה: "מלב דמשק לתל אביב - אנחנו כאן ולא נפחד מהאיומים שלכם. תראו אותנו עם שחר רועם, זהו אינו מפגן ראווה אלא אזהרות ישירות שתל אביב מבינה היטב".

​באחד העמודים נכתב: "במבצעי 'הרתעת התוקפנות' ששחררו את הערים הגדולות בסוריה בתוך 10 ימים, היו 3 חטיבות מיוחדות שהיוו את חוד החנית - לצד 'הלהקות האדומות' וחטיבות שאהין, היו 'גדודי ח'אלד בן אל-וליד', שהפכו כולם לעמוד השדרה של הצבא הסורי לאחר מיזוגם". מדובר בשלוש יחידות העילית: "הלהקות האדומות" (אל-עסאיב אל-חמראא), חטיבות "שאהין" - זרוע המל"טים והרחפנים של תחריר א-שאם, ובראשן "גדודי ח'אלד בן אל-וליד".

רקע כללי בהקשר: ​יחידת "הלהקות האדומות" הוקמה ב-2018 ככוח נוח'בה וחוד החנית למבצעים מיוחדים של ארגון הגג לפלגים הג'יהאדיסטים באידליב "היאת תחריר א-שאם" ואומנה בידי מדריכים צ'צ'נים מ"מלחמה טקטיקל" - יוצאי יחידות מובחרות בצבא הרוסי.

​מאוחר יותר, בשנת 2020, הוקמו "גדודי ח'אלד בן אל-וליד" ככוח נוח'בה מקביל המבוסס על לוחמים ערבים, שנועד לבצע פשיטות עומק ומארבים בהרים. הג'יהאדיסטים עברו כ-4 שנות הכשרה אינטנסיביות, הכוללות פשיטות ימיות בסירות גומי וצלילה, לחימת לילה בציוד תרמי, פריצה וכיבוש שטחים. בבליץ להפלת משטר אסד השתתפו כ-400 ג'יהאדיסטים מגדודי "ח'אלד בן אל-וליד"; הגדודים, בשילוב כוחות הנוח'בה הזרים שמנו כאלפים, היוו את חוד החנית בהפלת המשטר וחיסול מוקדי ההתנגדות המרכזיים באמצעות מעטפת אווירית של מל"טים מתאבדים ורחפנים של יחידת "שאהין", ולאחר מכן פשיטה קרקעית מהירה והסתערות אל תוך מוקדי הכוח של צבא אסד.

​כיום מוזגו כוחות הנוח'בה מהיחידות הללו כחוד החנית של הצבא הסורי של ג'ולאני: חלקם שולבו ככוח הקומנדו הימי בחיל הים הסורי, וחלקם בחטיבות הנוח'בה וחוד החנית של כוחות נוח'בה היבשה. בעמודים מדגישים כי מדובר בכוחות ייעודיים ללוחמת גרילה, פשיטה ולוחמה בשטח בנוי - ומתארים אותם כ"סיוט המרכזי של נתניהו וישותו".
